Long time single-malt drinker who switched primarily to bourbon. I started drinking single malts 20 years or so ago, when I was living in Europe. Had access to a variety at good prices and just kept growing my collection. I quickly determined that I was not a fan of Highland malts which mostly seemed one-dimensional. Became a big fan of Islay, especially Lagavulin (duh). When I moved back to the USA (15 years ago), I did a lot of driving through Kentucky so I decided to start trying bourbon. I even took a tasting class and went on some distillery tours. There's a world of difference between Single Malt and it's Kentucky cousin, but I immediately appreciated the quality of good Bourbon. And Bourbon is very inexpensive here in the USA (at least where I live) compared to the better Single Malts.

I still have quite a lot of great Single Malt, but now my Bourbon collection is just as robust. In fact, Bourbon is now my drink of choice. My personal favorite is Blanton's (and yes, I've got some VanWinkle). Elijah Craig is the absolute best "budget" Bourbon for me. I should add that I never mix drinks--that's for college kids. Whiskey/Bourbon should be drank with (at most) a couple cubes of ice--that's it. It's a fucking sin to pollute good alcohol with sugar.
